Finca Las Margaritas is based on extensive volcanic wasteland that since 3 or 4 million years ago covered the coastal platform of Las Galletas. In this large agricultural area of 825 Ha is located the largest bananas plantations in greenhouse of Tenerife, where moves a volume of more than 26 thousand tons for export anually. FINCA LAS MARGARITAS began with the cultivation of banana in Las Galletas in the year 1977, the union and several family members of Adolfo Guerra González entrepreneurship and Margarita Hernández Pérez, later named the estate, being 86 years old in 2012. Both came from a long family generation of farmers in S/C de La Palma and San Andrés y Sauces. On this farm are produces 2 cultivars of Canary Island banana, the great dwarf and the thick Palm or small dwarf, the Dwarf Cavendish variety, reaching an average of 45-50 klg per bunch, and can find copies that they exceed the 70 klg. The acreage is of approximately 7 Ha with 98% of bananas and 2% of fruit trees such as: mango, papaya and avocado.

The Ethnographic Park & Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar is a large open-air museum and one of the five official botanical gardens of the Canary Islands. The Park was founded in 1998 by the renowned Norwegian researcher Thor Heyerdahl, who was responsible for safeguarding the pyramids from an urban development plan. In addition to the pyramids, the Park includes four outdoor trails and specialised gardens, spread over more than 64,000m2. The routes allow visitors to stroll freely through the extensive gardens, discovering interesting aspects of Canarian culture and nature. These routes include a Canarian Botanical Route, a Cultural Route and a Volcanic Route. The facilities also include the Casa Chacona Museum and an Auditorium.  As for its botanical collections, you can visit the Poison Garden, unique in Spain, and the Sustainable Garden, a reproduction of a Canarian ravine, including a watercourse and presenting the flora characteristic of these environments in a sustainable way. The Tropicarium shows the life strategies used by orchids and insectivorous plants to survive in tropical conditions. The Park was the winner of the 'Best Overall Sustainable Tourism Practice 2021' award for the island of Tenerife and a national finalist in the 'Remarkable Venue Awards 2022' in the Best Hidden Gem category, which highlights the most outstanding and special places for travellers from all over the world. The Park has also been awarded the Biosphere Committed distinction for its sustainable commitment and is a member of the Climate Heritage Network. The Ethnographic Park & Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar offers a unique outdoor experience, without crowds of people thanks to its 30,000m2 of accessible garden areas, allowing culture and nature lovers to enjoy a day outdoors in a different, safe and sustainable environment.

San Blas Reserve is an open-air museum, where you can explore archaeological sites, ancient caves, and historical remains that reveal what life was like on the island centuries ago. More than 4 million years ago, lava flows shaped this unique volcanic landscape, later sculpted by wind and water into what is now known as the breathtaking “lunar landscape” of San Blas. The visit includes access to an innovative Interpretation Center, equipped with advanced interactive rooms and immersive audiovisual experiences. Here, you will discover the secrets of San Blas' geology, biodiversity, and history in a fun and educational way. Immerse yourself in a journey where nature, history, and technology come together to create an unforgettable adventure in the heart of Tenerife’s volcanic landscape. Book now and uncover one of Tenerife’s best-kept secrets!

The Parque del Drago is the first park in the Canary Islands with native flora with representations of the different bioclimatic levels of the northwest of Tenerife. In this "nature classroom" located in Icod de Los Vinos you will find ethnographic areas of special interest such as a medicinal garden with plants used by the island's ancestors as natural remedies. A "carbonera", which was the traditional way of obtaining charcoal and which was a very important resource on the island. A wine press, or a cave where you can admire the representation of an aboriginal burial. And the star of the place: the spectacular Millenian Dragon Tree, the longest living tree of its species and a national monument since 1917.

The San Miguel Castle is an impressive construction of 6,000 square metres and made of Canarian canto stone, with principal towers of more than 16 metres in height and an extensive area of 20,000 square metres .From the moment you enter the grounds, you find yourself in an authentic medieval world. The entrance is decorated with historical armour, swords, chests and scrolls of the medieval epoch. The Count, Don Rodrigo, and his daughter, the young Countess, will greet you and welcome you to their Castle. The kind subjects of Count Rodrigo will guide you to the Tournament Hall, where the complex show of medieval fights and games will take placein the presence of the Counts in their Royal box seats. During the Tournament, you will be served the banquet just as it was done in medieval times; The soup is drunk and an entire chicken per person with its garnish is eaten by hand.The dinner is completed with dessert and beverages. The Count´s guests are seated in stands of long tables and benches where the visibility is optimal from anywhere in the Tournament Hall. The sand arena where the horses and knights will perform is of 50 metres in long. The Hall has a capacity of 1100 guests.Usually after the Tournaments, the guests move to adjourn to a second hall which has a capacity for 800 guests. The Ballroom, as Count Rodrigo calls it, has a large stage where the guests can dance, where any type of performance can be arranged: Orchestra, Comedians, Acrobatics, Spanish Ballet, etc.

In addition to recreating the best classic and contemporary choreographies, "History" performs live renditions of the most beautiful film and theater soundtracks, while also celebrating the wonderful musicals of Broadway. This live music, dance, theater, and acrobatics show is suitable for all ages and nationalities, offering an unforgettable experience for all who attend. Join us on this journey through the history of music!

Tenerife, with its crystal-clear waters and abundant marine life, is the ideal place for bottom fishing from a boat. This activity, perfect for catching species such as groupers, snappers, and moray eels, requires specialized equipment like rods, reels, hooks, and bait, along with a suitable boat. Mastering techniques such as choosing the right bait and identifying the best fishing spots in Tenerife is essential for a rewarding experience. Having an expert captain ensures a safe and enriching adventure, suitable for both beginners and seasoned fishing enthusiasts. Book your bottom fishing excursion in Tenerife through our platform and experience the thrill of fishing in one of the Atlantic’s most captivating destinations.

The Yate Sofía is one of the pioneering companies offering big game fishing excursions in Tenerife, with a history dating back to 1967, when they began taking the first tourists on fishing trips and cruises in the waters of the island’s southern coast. This vessel, a STRIKER 44, is built with robust marine-grade aluminum and features a hull specifically designed for deep-sea fishing, providing a safe, high-quality experience for fishing enthusiasts. Yate Sofía maintains a daily communication network with the local professional fishing fleet, allowing them to track the movement of tuna in real time and head to the best fishing spots each day. The primary fishing technique used is surface trolling, ideal for catching large species such as marlin, tuna, wahoo, and mahi-mahi, among others. Enjoy a unique fishing experience in the Canary Islands, sharing in-depth knowledge and passion for deep sea fishing in Tenerife with a professional and reliable team.

Macaronesian Divers is a unique experience centre in an extraordinary setting, the bay of Radazul, located just 8 minutes from Santa Cruz de Tenerife, the capital of the island.   Created by divers and for divers, and designed for your enjoyment during training and skills acquisition or simply to admire the coastline and its great diversity of multilevel dives: from the first dive to the most radical technical dive.

Introducing “Royal Boat”, a luxury American ship ready to sail you across the seas of Tenerife in an unbeatable fishing experience. A boat trip to enjoy fishing and nature, the sun and marine fauna. Enjoy an exciting private fishing experience with your family or friends on the “Royal Garden Boat”. The outing begins at the Puerto Colón pier, from where we’ll head to the deeper waters near the coast. The Canary Islands are considered one of the best locations in the world to find large species thanks to the Atlantic currents. It’s one of the few places where you can catch bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna, bigeye tuna, blue marlin, white marlin, spearfish, dorado, barracuda and more. If you prefer deep-sea fishing, the Canary Islands have excellent sea beds for this type of fishing. Here you can fish different species, such as the greater amberjack, dentex, sama, comber, blackbelly rosefish and grouper.

Enjoy one of our adrenaline kicking activities: Parascending: Enjoy the amazing views 80 metres (260 feets) above Tenerife's Coast. Kayaking has become one of the most popular water activities in recent years. It's easy and fun, you don't need any previous experience. The tour lasts 2 hours and includes 30 minutes snorkelling with turtles. Each client is given a snorkel kit, waistcoats and swimming boots. First we do the briefing and then we start from the beach in front of our school in Los Cristianos and head to the cliffs of PalmMar. You will be impressed not only with the breathtaking views of the surroundings, but also with the animals you will encounter. There are many dolphins living in the area and they are always willing to come up to the kayaks and swim alongside. We make a stop in front of the PalmMar rocks and go on a snorkelling tour to find beautiful canary turtles. This place is home to a lot of fish and animals that you will observe from the surface. You can definitely be sure that you will have an amazing time.

Explore hidden beaches and protected natural areas near Caleta de Adeje on a Stand Up Paddle (SUP) trip. Discover secret corners while snorkelling in crystal clear waters. Ideal for those who are looking for adventure and connection with nature in Tenerife. The activity is divided into 3 stages: First, the team will provide you with the paddle board, life jacket and paddle, as well as an explanation of the places you will visit. You will learn the safety rules and the basic notions necessary for the practice of paddle surfing, which you will practice in the water before the route. Once you have acquired the basic knowledge, the adventure begins, exploring the most beautiful landscapes of the south of Tenerife. To make the most of the experience, you will have snorkelling equipment at your disposal to explore the marine landscape of these volcanic coves. The route of the trip will depend on the level of the group. Basic: Ideal for beginners, this tour focuses on teaching and practising basic snorkelling techniques. It includes a trip to the nearby beach of Los Morteros. Intermediate: For those with previous SUP experience. Offers a moderate challenge including visits to Los Morteros and the next beach, Diego Hernandez. Advanced: Intended for participants with advanced SUP skills, this is the most challenging tour. It includes a visit to Puertito de Adeje, a picturesque fishing village on the south coast of Tenerife.

From there, the route heads towards the impressive Masca Gorge , one of Tenerife's most iconic locations, where you can enjoy unparalleled panoramic views and a stunning natural environment. An ideal activity for couples, groups of friends and sea lovers who want to discover Tenerife from a different perspective.

The Pascua Florida festival in Guía de Isora is one of the most emblematic cultural events of Holy Week in southern Tenerife . Every year, the historic center of this town is transformed into a spectacular open-air museum where floral art, tradition, and creativity come together to offer a unique experience in the Canary Islands. During Holy Thursday and Easter Sunday, the streets of Guía de Isora are transformed into an artistic procession featuring stunning floral creations crafted by florists and artists. These works reinterpret the Passion of Christ through ephemeral compositions that combine color, symbolism, and design. The Easter Flower Festival in Guía de Isora is a benchmark for cultural tourism in Tenerife . Each floral arrangement is unique and unrepeatable , making this event one of the most singular cultural experiences on the island during Holy Week. Visiting the Easter celebrations in Guía de Isora means discovering a tradition that blends art, spirituality, and historical heritage in the heart of southern Tenerife. It's an event that surprises, moves, and attracts visitors each year who seek to experience Holy Week in Tenerife from an artistic and unique perspective.

On this half-day excursion youll have the opportunity to explore the largest and oldest National Park in the Canary Islands and return to your hotel to enjoy the rest of the day.   Youll enjoy a journey from the coast to the highest point in Tenerife, passing through Canary pine forests and traditional villages such as Vilafor.   As we continue along the path, well venture into volcanoes and rivers of petrified lava. Well make a few stops so you can admire one of the worlds largest calderas: Las Cañadas del Teide. Well visit Los Roques de García at the foot of Spains highest peak: Mount Teide, at 3,718 meters above sea level. This imposing volcano, located in the heart of Tenerife, is the main reason why Teide National Park, declared in 1954, is the most visited national park in Europe. This excursion does not include the option of riding the Teide cable car or visiting its base. Finally, we will resume our hike and continue admiring everything this incredible natural space has to offer on the way back.

On this tour we will spend a full day touring the most representative places in the north of Tenerife. Our first visit will be to the Teide National Park, located in the heart of Tenerife and home to the highest peak in Spain: the volcano El Teide. Here we will stop for about 30 minutes to admire the impressive volcanic landscapes of Las Cañadas del Teide, not forgetting the emblematic Roques de García. After this visit, we will descend to Icod de los Vinos where we will have the opportunity to contemplate the famous Drago Milenario, which is said to be more than 800 years old. You will have free time to have lunch on your own or enjoy the Canarian gastronomy tasting one of the menus that we recommend in some of the restaurants in the area. The next destination is Garachico, a colourful coastal village with a history marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. Here we will stroll through the streets of its historic quarter, recognised as a Cultural Heritage Site and one of the most representative of the Canary Islands, and discover emblematic sites such as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by lava flows, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that defended the town from pirate attacks. We will follow the route and enter the vibrant nature of the Teno Rural Park until we reach the hamlet of Masca, located between impressive valleys and ravines. Let yourself be surprised by the charm of the traditional architecture of this enclave, declared a Site of Ethnographic and Historical Interest and an Asset of Cultural Interest.

Flavors and Wines of Tenerife: A Journey for the Senses On this excursion through southern Tenerife, you will discover the island's most authentic flavors and renowned wines, with the convenience of returning to your accommodation in time to continue enjoying your day. We will start with a visit to Finca Las Margaritas, where you will learn about traditional banana cultivation and taste products made with gofio, palm honey, and tropical fruits. Then, we will enjoy the breathtaking views along the mountain road to Vilaflor, until we reach Bodega Lagar de Chasna, where we will have a wine tasting paired with a delicious selection of the best Canarian gastronomy. After this experience, we will return so you can make the most of the rest of your day.

Would you like to discover the island of La Gomera on a single day trip from Tenerife? Then this is your perfect option! Our day starts by heading to the port of Los Cristianos, where we will take a ferry to the island. Once here, we'll board the bus and head into the Hermigua Valley, where we'll have the opportunity to capture some photos of the breathtaking scenery. We will continue the excursion until we reach the municipality of Agulo, where we will enjoy a delicious lunch in a typical restaurant with local products. If availability permits, during lunch we will witness a live demonstration of "silbo gomero", a unique language declared Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO. After lunch we will enter the Garajonay National Park, a paradise of laurel forests and a nature reserve also declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Laguna Grande we will learn all the curiosities of this magical place where it is said that the witches of the island used to meet. We will make a stop at the imposing Roque de Agando, one of the most emblematic places of La Gomera. Finally, we will arrive in San Sebastián, the capital of the island. Here we will have the opportunity to discover the last traces left by Christopher Columbus after his passage through La Gomera, such as the Torre del Conde or the Casa Colón. Once we have finished our visit of San Sebastian, we will head back to the ferry to Tenerife.

This excursion gives you the opportunity to get to know the essence of Tenerife in just one day. We will start the day by visiting Candelaria. This coastal town is home to the Basilica of Candelaria, one of the most important places of worship in Tenerife. On the seashore you can admire the imposing bronze statues commemorating the ancient Guanche Kings of Tenerife. The excursion continues in the Historic-Artistic Site of La Villa de La Orotava. The cobbled streets of its historic quarter will take us to places full of charm and culture such as La Casa de Los Balcones, the Town Hall Square or the Church of Nuestra Señora de La Concepción. We will continue our journey through the north of Tenerife until we reach Garachico, a charming coastal town, whose history is marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. We will stroll through its historic centre, declared a Site of Cultural Interest, and visit such emblematic places as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by volcanic lava, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that protected the town from pirate attacks. Here you will have free time to have lunch on your own or taste the Canarian gastronomy in one of the restaurants we recommend. After this visit, we will enter the Teno Rural Park where we will enjoy its impressive natural landscapes. Its winding roads will take us to Masca, a hamlet surrounded by spectacular cliffs that preserves its traditional Canarian architecture.

This excursion perfectly blends history, culture, and nature. Discover Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Anaga, and San Cristóbal de La Laguna: three must-see gems in the north of Tenerife. Our first stop will be in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, the capital of the island. We will stroll through its vibrant streets, leading us to its most iconic spots, such as Plaza de España, Plaza Weyler, or the Mercado de Nuestra Señora de África. Next, we will venture into the Anaga massif, an impressive natural area declared a Biosphere Reserve by UNESCO in 2015 due to its extraordinary biodiversity. Here, you can enjoy some of its most representative viewpoints, like the Mirador de la Jardina or the Mirador Cruz del Carmen, offering spectacular views of the island. Finally, we will continue to San Cristóbal de La Laguna, the first city founded in Tenerife after its conquest and a historic gem declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1999. We will walk through its historic and culturally rich streets, discovering its most significant monuments, such as the Cathedral of San Cristóbal de La Laguna or Plaza del Adelantado. You will have time to enjoy lunch and taste the delicious Canarian cuisine in one of the charming restaurants in the city. After a day of discovering several of Tenerife's treasures, we will return to the pickup points. We will continue our journey into the Anaga mountain range, a stunning natural area declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015 due to its extraordinary biodiversity. Here, we will visit some of its most iconic viewpoints, such as the Mirador de la Jardina and the Mirador Cruz del Carmen. After a day exploring some of Tenerife's treasures, we will return to the pickup points.

On this excursion you will have the opportunity to enjoy a relaxing day, stroll around and choose what to see, do and where to sunbathe and swim. We will start our day by going to the south of Tenerife, specifically to Los Cristianos, a place that maintains its seafaring charm. It is the centre of commercial and cultural activity in the region, and numerous maritime connections depart from its port. In addition, every Tuesday and Sunday, there is a street market with a wide variety of products. You will have the whole day free to enjoy this area at your leisure. If your aim is to enjoy a wonderful day at the beach, you will have both Playa de Las Vistas and Playa de Los Cristianos at your disposal. Take the opportunity to go for a dip, or stroll around the shopping area. In the afternoon, we will meet in Los Cristianos to head to the north of the island and return to the pick-up points.

Discover with us the charming town of Puerto de la Cruz, located in the coastal area of the Orotava Valley, in the north of Tenerife. You will have the whole day at your leisure to enjoy a pleasant day by the sea and discover all that this town has to offer. Despite its popularity with travellers who visit the island every year, Puerto de la Cruz has not lost its seaside charm. You can stroll through its beautiful streets and squares, such as the Plaza del Charco or the Muelle Viejo. Many people believe that one of the most outstanding attractions of the municipality is its mild climate that is maintained throughout the year, a fact that was described by several European naturalists who visited Puerto de la Cruz in the 18th and 19th centuries. You will have the opportunity to walk around the city and discover such emblematic places as the Botanical Gardens or the spectacular Martiánez Lake, and end the day watching the waves break on the coast of San Telmo.
